subject: Access controls (RBAC, support access, break-glass) - follow-up
messages:
From: Tom Lopez <tom.lopez@fintrust.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
Cc: priya.shah@fintrust.com
Date: Mon, 17 Aug 2026 14:22:00 -0400
Subject: Access controls questions after demo

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the demo today.

I appreciate the walkthrough. The security and infosec team had a few follow-up questions specific to access controls and support access before we move forward:

- RBAC: can you share the granularity of roles you support? We need role->resource mapping examples (who can see customer prompts/outputs, who can view request logs).
- Least privilege: do you have built-in least-privilege templates or recommendations for common roles (engineer, SRE, support)?
- Support access / break-glass: what is your process for Redwood support to access customer data during incidents? Are there JIT approvals, audit logs, and time-limited sessions?
- Audit/logging: retention windows for logs (auth, request/response logs), and whether logs are accessible to customers or only provided via export.
- Data residency & PII handling: we briefly touched on this can you confirm if customer data can be restricted to a US region and whether you support masking/PII scrubbing at ingest?

If you have any reference docs (RBAC matrix, break-glass playbook, SOC2 artifacts) that would help our security reviewers that would be great. Also happy to jump on a 30-min call with the security team if easier.

Thanks,
Tom
Tom Lopez
Director, Security Engineering
FinTrust

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: Access controls questions after demo

Tom,

Thanks for the notes and great questions. Quick recap from our call + answers and next steps below.

Recap / high-level answers:
- RBAC: Redwood supports role-based policies scoped to resources (model endpoint, project, dataset). We provide a default set of roles (Admin, Engineer, SRE, Support, ReadOnly) and customers can add custom roles. See attached RBAC matrix for examples mapping roles to typical privileges (view logs, manage keys, invoke endpoints, view request payloads).
- Least privilege: we recommend starting with the ReadOnly or Support-lite roles and granting invoke or manage permissions explicitly. Our console has templates for common setups (engineering, platform, support).
- Support access & break-glass: Redwood support requires a documented request, approval from customer-designated approvers (can be automated via a JIT integration), and sessions are time-bound with session tokens. All support sessions are logged and recorded in the audit trail. Break-glass requests trigger elevated logging and an automated email to the security contacts.
- Audit/logging: Auth logs and admin activity are retained by default for 90 days; request/response logs retention is configurable per account (default 30 days). We can export logs to your preferred SIEM or S3 bucket for longer-term retention.
- Data residency & PII: We support region pinning for hosted projects (US, EU currently). PII scrubbing and automatic token-redaction at ingest are available as configurable options; we can also apply custom regex filters via our data processing pipeline.

Attachments I'm sharing:
- redwood_rbac_matrix_v2.xlsx (example role->privilege mapping)
- break_glass_playbook.pdf (high-level process + audit hooks)

Next steps (proposed):
1) I'll loop in Dylan (our infra/security engineer) to answer any detailed technical questions.
2) If you can confirm the desired log retention window and whether you need request/response logs stored >90 days, we'll prepare a tailored configuration and pricing impact.
3) I can set up a 30-min technical review with your security team this week — Wednesday/Thursday 10-2 PT. Please let me know a time.

If you need SOC2 artifacts we can provide redacted evidence and an auditor contact under an NDA. I'll follow up separately on that.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0199
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Access controls questions after demo (tech details)

Hi Tom / Marissa,

Looping in a couple of technical details that usually come up with customers like FinTrust.

Support access / break-glass (details):
- Access model: Support access is only possible with an explicit ticket that includes customer approval. For customers who prefer automation we support an Okta-based JIT approval flow (SCIM + OAuth) that can require an approver to click to approve a session.
- Session controls: When a support session is approved we issue a short-lived session token (max 1 hour by default) scoped to the minimum privileges required. All commands executed during the session are recorded.
- Audit trail: Session start/stop, commands, and any data viewed are written to the audit log with a session id. Logs include requester identity, approver identity, and IP. Customers can stream these logs to their SIEM via our log export connector (Kafka, S3, or syslog).
- Break-glass escalation: Break-glass creates an elevated event that (a) emails security contacts, (b) increases logging verbosity for the affected project, and (c) produces an automated incident report (PDF) that we can push to a pre-configured bucket.

RBAC & least privilege (config knobs):
- Role templates: Admin, Dev, Platform, Support-lite, ReadOnly. Each template is editable and we expose a role API so infra teams can codify role creation in IaC.
- Resource scoping: Roles are evaluated against resource tags (project:id, env:prod/stage). We recommend scoping support roles to non-prod by default and enabling prod only for specific, time-limited tickets.

Logging retention / exports:
- Default: auth/admin 90d, request/response 30d.
- Options: Custom retention up to 7 years via export to customer-controlled S3.

Attachments: I attached the latest RBAC matrix and the break-glass playbook we use for on-call runbooks. Also adding a SOC2 artifact stub (redacted).

Drive folder with templates: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRBAC

Happy to jump on a call with your security team to walk through the playbook and run through an example JIT approval.

— Dylan Brooks
Infra Security Engineer | Redwood Inference
